changeSet.comment: nexus.topic_assignments.doc_id: TEXT -> bytea. A DO-block precheck (SELECT count(*) + RAISE EXCEPTION, NOT an inline CASE inside the ALTER's USING clause — corrected 2026-08-17, critic Sig-1) runs first and asserts every row is canonical-64-hex (D0.9 wedge-proofing, HAL directive 2026-08-16: never wedge on residual garbage, but never silently admit it either) even though P3b's cleanup already guarantees every surviving row is conformant one changeset earlier in the same walk. Only then does the second sql element run the ALTER with a bare `USING decode(doc_id, 'hex')`. ANALYZE in the same pass (D0.5) — the PK and doc_id indexes rebuild automatically. See this file's header for the full derivation.
changeSet.sql: -- RDR-194 critical fix round 2 (2026-08-17, bead nexus-7ec4i, P0). RDR-180 -- precedent (rdr180-1-drop-dependent-views): nexus.diag_chash_conformance -- (src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py, nexus.db.chash_tables.diag_conformance_ -- view_ddl) references doc_id as one of its DEBT_CHASH_TABLES legs -- -- Postgres refuses ALTER COLUMN TYPE on a column a view depends on -- ("cannot alter type of a column used by a view or rule") REGARDLESS OF -- WHO OWNS THE VIEW -- this is a structural dependency restriction, not a -- permissions check (verified empirically: a table-owning, non-view-owning -- role hits the identical "cannot alter type" error a plain DROP-then-ALTER -- would). GENERAL ownership defense, not a claim about any one deployment's -- current state (measured 2026-08-17: conexus's cloud cluster carries NO -- such view at all, and every view in schema nexus there is already -- migration-role-owned -- the view most likely never existed on cloud, the -- provisioning path being table-existence-gated and its heal path dead -- code). The edge this defends is a DIFFERENT install shape: an OLDER LOCAL -- install where pg_provision's superuser bootstrap DID succeed in creating -- the view before this migration ever ran, or a BYO-Postgres DBA install -- that followed docs/configuration.md's (superuser-oriented) DDL. This -- migration role does not own such a view, so a bare `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS` -- would raise `insufficient_privilege` ("must be owner of view") -- IF -- EXISTS only suppresses the object-ABSENT error class, never an ownership -- error. Unlike taxonomy-011-8's CREATE OR REPLACE / GRANT (which CAN -- gracefully skip on a foreign owner, since nothing else in that changeset -- depends on the view's existence), a graceful skip here is NOT viable: -- if the DROP is merely skipped and the walk proceeds, the very next -- statement (the ALTER below) hits the SAME structural block anyway -- -- proven above, this is not owner-conditional -- aborting this changeset -- regardless, just via a generic, unnamed Postgres error instead of a -- diagnosable one. So the catch below RAISES, not just NOTICEs: it turns -- an opaque failure into a NAMED, actionable one (D0.9 wedge-proofing, -- the same philosophy as this changeset's own doc_id shape guard above -- -- fail loud with a remedy, never silently tolerate or half-apply). The -- doc_id TYPE bytea conversion genuinely CANNOT proceed while any view -- depends on the column, so this changeset correctly still fails when the -- edge fires; the fix is operational (drop the foreign view first), not a -- workaround this migration role can perform on its own. DO $$ BEGIN BEGIN DROP VIEW IF EXISTS nexus.diag_chash_conformance; EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'RDR-194 P3c (nexus-tk070.p3c, nexus-7ec4i): nexus.diag_chash_conformance exists but this migration role does not own it and cannot drop it. The doc_id TYPE bytea conversion below cannot proceed while ANY view depends on doc_id, regardless of ownership -- PostgreSQL refuses ALTER COLUMN TYPE whenever a dependent view exists. Remedy: the view''s owning role (typically a superuser, e.g. the local bundle''s bootstrap identity, or a BYO-Postgres DBA''s own role) must run DROP VIEW IF EXISTS nexus.diag_chash_conformance, then retry this migration -- taxonomy-011-8, later in this same walk, recreates it owned by this migration role with security_invoker, closing this permanently.'; END; END $$;

changeSet.comment: nexus.assign_from_chashes_384: doc_id INSERT target moves from hex text (n.m_chash) to raw bytes (n.m_chash_bytes, = c.chash directly, no encode/decode). RETURNS TABLE(chash text, ...) wire contract unchanged -- RETURN QUERY still projects n.m_chash (hex). Layered CREATE OR REPLACE over taxonomy-009-1 (the LIVE generation, not vectors-005-16). Rollback deliberately empty (D0.6) -- see this file's header, "ROLLBACK ORDERING".
changeSet.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus.assign_from_chashes_384( p_collection text, p_chashes text[], p_cross_collection boolean ) RETURNS TABLE( chash text, topic_id bigint, similarity double precision ) LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $fn$ #variable_conflict use_column BEGIN IF p_cross_collection THEN INSERT INTO nexus.catalog_collections (tenant_id, name) VALUES (current_setting('nexus.tenant', true), p_collection) ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, name) DO NOTHING;
RETURN QUERY WITH nearest AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ON (c.chash) encode(c.chash, 'hex') AS m_chash, c.chash AS m_chash_bytes, ct.topic_id AS m_topic_id, (1 - (c.embedding_384 <=> ct.embedding_384))::double precision AS m_sim FROM nexus.chunks c JOIN nexus.taxonomy_centroids ct ON ct.collection <> p_collection AND ct.embedding_384 IS NOT NULL WHERE c.collection = p_collection AND c.embedding_384 IS NOT NULL AND c.chash = ANY(ARRAY(SELECT decode(x, 'hex') FROM unnest(p_chashes) x)) ORDER BY c.chash, (c.embedding_384 <=> ct.embedding_384) ASC, ct.collection ASC, ct.topic_id ASC ), persisted AS ( INSERT INTO nexus.topic_assignments AS ta (tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by, similarity, assigned_at, source_collection) SELECT current_setting('nexus.tenant', true), n.m_chash_bytes, n.m_topic_id, 'projection', n.m_sim, now(), p_collection FROM nearest n ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id) DO UPDATE SET similarity = GREATEST(COALESCE(ta.similarity, -1.0), EXCLUDED.similarity), assigned_at = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.similarity > COALESCE(ta.similarity, -1.0) THEN EXCLUDED.assigned_at ELSE ta.assigned_at END, source_collection = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.similarity > COALESCE(ta.similarity, -1.0) THEN EXCLUDED.source_collection ELSE ta.source_collection END, assigned_by = 'projection' RETURNING 1 ) SELECT n.m_chash, n.m_topic_id, n.m_sim FROM nearest n; ELSE RETURN QUERY WITH nearest AS ( SELECT DISTINCT ON (c.chash) encode(c.chash, 'hex') AS m_chash, c.chash AS m_chash_bytes, ct.topic_id AS m_topic_id, (1 - (c.embedding_384 <=> ct.embedding_384))::double precision AS m_sim FROM nexus.chunks c JOIN nexus.taxonomy_centroids ct ON ct.collection = p_collection AND ct.embedding_384 IS NOT NULL WHERE c.collection = p_collection AND c.embedding_384 IS NOT NULL AND c.chash = ANY(ARRAY(SELECT decode(x, 'hex') FROM unnest(p_chashes) x)) ORDER BY c.chash, (c.embedding_384 <=> ct.embedding_384) ASC, ct.topic_id ASC ), persisted AS ( INSERT INTO nexus.topic_assignments (tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by, source_collection) SELECT current_setting('nexus.tenant', true), n.m_chash_bytes, n.m_topic_id, 'centroid', p_collection FROM nearest n ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING 1 ) SELECT n.m_chash, n.m_topic_id, NULL::double precision FROM nearest n; END IF; END; $fn$;

changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus.search_topic_scoped_384( p_query vector(384), p_topic_label text, p_collection text, p_n int ) RETURNS TABLE(id text, content text, collection text, distance float8) LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER AS $$ SELECT encode(c.chash, 'hex'), c.chunk_text, c.collection, (c.embedding_384 <=> p_query)::float8 FROM nexus.chunks c JOIN nexus.topic_assignments ta ON ta.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND ta.doc_id = c.chash JOIN nexus.topics t ON t.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND t.id = ta.topic_id WHERE c.collection = p_collection AND t.collection = p_collection AND t.label = p_topic_label AND c.embedding_384 IS NOT NULL AND (NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks m WHERE m.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND m.chash = c.chash) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks m JOIN nexus.catalog_documents d ON d.tenant_id = m.tenant_id AND d.tumbler = m.doc_id WHERE m.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND m.chash = c.chash AND d.deleted_at IS NULL)) ORDER BY c.embedding_384 <=> p_query LIMIT p_n $$;

changeSet.author: nexus-tk070.p3c
changeSet.comment: Liquibase-owned `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW nexus.diag_chash_ conformance` (critical fix round 2026-08-17, critic Sig-2 / bead nexus-i3k3e's Sig-2 finding): changeset 1 above DROPs this view and its own header/comment claimed `pg_provision` would recreate it "best-effort on the next provision/service-start pass" — a claim that was FALSE for any deployment where nothing ever calls `reprovision_diag_view_best_effort()` again (dead code, zero callers). This changeset closes that hole for good: the SAME text `nexus.db.chash_tables.diag_conformance_view_ddl()` generates (now `WITH (security_invoker = true)`, which is what makes a Liquibase-owned view — created as `nexus_admin`, NOSUPERUSER, no BYPASSRLS — still count every tenant's rows correctly for `nexus_diag`, BYPASSRLS, regardless of who owns the view; see that function's own docstring for the full derivation), plus a role-existence-guarded `GRANT SELECT` mirroring `grants-nexus-diag-3`'s shape exactly. `runAlways` self-heals both the view and the grant on every boot, closing the reprovisioning gap permanently rather than once. See this file's header, "WHAT SHIPS" item 8 and "ROLLBACK ORDERING", for the full derivation and how this interacts with changeset 1's own rollback. `pg_provision`'s superuser path is untouched (see its own docstring for the narrow window it remains the only creator for, and what of bead nexus-7shei is still open).
changeSet.sql:
DO $$ BEGIN -- Nested BEGIN/EXCEPTION (2026-08-17, critical fix round, critic -- Sig-1/-2): a PRE-EXISTING FOREIGN-OWNED view (e.g. pg_provision's -- own superuser-owned view, still live on an install this changeset -- has not yet converged with; or a DBA-provisioned managed-deployment -- copy) makes this role's CREATE OR REPLACE fail with -- insufficient_privilege ("must be owner of view ..."), NOT -- duplicate_table -- REPLACE never raises "already exists". Catching -- it here means a foreign-owned view degrades to a graceful skip -- (that owner's existing definition stands) rather than aborting the -- ENTIRE migration walk -- the same no-wedge ethos this whole -- critical fix round exists to enforce, applied to this changeset's -- own new DDL. A nested BEGIN/EXCEPTION block creates an implicit -- savepoint, so the catch does not abort the surrounding changeset's -- transaction. BEGIN CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW nexus.diag_chash_conformance WITH (security_invoker = true) AS SELECT 'nexus.chunks' AS table_name, count(*) AS non_conformant FROM nexus.chunks WHERE octet_length(chash) <> 32 UNION ALL SELECT 'nexus.catalog_document_chunks' AS table_name, count(*) AS non_conformant FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks WHERE octet_length(chash) <> 32 UNION ALL SELECT 'nexus.topic_assignments' AS table_name, count(*) AS non_conformant FROM nexus.topic_assignments t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks c WHERE c.chash = t.doc_id) UNION ALL SELECT 'nexus.frecency' AS table_name, count(*) AS non_conformant FROM nexus.frecency t WHERE t.chunk_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]+$' AND length(t.chunk_id) % 2 = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks c WHERE c.chash = decode(t.chunk_id, 'hex')) UNION ALL SELECT 'nexus.relevance_log' AS table_name, count(*) AS non_conformant FROM nexus.relevance_log t WHERE t.chunk_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]+$' AND length(t.chunk_id) % 2 = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks c WHERE c.chash = decode(t.chunk_id, 'hex')); EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege THEN RAISE NOTICE 'nexus.diag_chash_conformance already exists with a foreign (non-migration-role) owner -- skipping CREATE OR REPLACE; that owner''s existing definition stands and self-heals automatically if that owner ever drops it'; END;
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'nexus_diag') THEN RAISE NOTICE 'nexus_diag absent — diag view grant skipped (created by pg_provision/DBA; self-heals next boot)'; ELSE -- Same foreign-owner degrade as above: GRANT on a relation this -- role does not own also raises insufficient_privilege, not a -- hard requirement -- the foreign owner's own GRANT (pg_provision -- already issues one for the view IT creates) covers nexus_diag -- in that case instead. BEGIN GRANT SELECT ON nexus.diag_chash_conformance TO nexus_diag; EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege THEN RAISE NOTICE 'cannot GRANT SELECT on a foreign-owned nexus.diag_chash_conformance -- its owner must grant nexus_diag directly (matches what the pg_provision superuser path already does for the view it creates)'; END; END IF; END $$;
